body.x: Le Café du Geek, a French technology and lifestyle outlet, named BEYLESS, Brain-Life Link and Tesollo Inc. its top three innovative companies at the FIX 2026 Global Media Awards.

The Future Innovation tech eXpo 2026 (FIX 2026) ran from Oct. 21 to Oct. 24 at EXCO in Daegu, featuring future mobility, robotics, and AI and ICT technologies and products. Under the theme "AI, Beyond Tech Into Reality," the third edition combined the Daegu International Future Auto & Mobility Expo (DIFA), the Daegu Robot Expo (ROBEX), the ICT Convergence Expo Korea (ITCE) and start-up programs. In the Global Media Awards, overseas outlets review technologies and products on the show floor, and each outlet chooses its own top three companies.

Le Café du Geek delivers global technology news and product reviews to French-speaking readers. It tests products in real-world conditions and examines their practicality and value to consumers. Leo Thevenet, the outlet's editor-in-chief, first attended DIFA 2023, the predecessor of FIX, and has returned as a global media partner for FIX 2024, FIX 2025 and FIX 2026.

body.x: The three companies cover automotive software, everyday brain-state monitoring and precise robotic manipulation.
BEYLESS Develops Embedded Software for Future Mobility

BEYLESS Co., Ltd., led by CEO Hyungjun Kim, develops embedded software and vehicle electronics systems for automotive use. Its work covers software-defined vehicles (SDVs) and in-vehicle infotainment (IVI), and it offers AUTOSAR-based software and over-the-air (OTA) updates.

As vehicles become electrified and intelligent, more of their functions run on software. That makes it more important to connect multiple electronic control units and software reliably and to update them continuously. BEYLESS develops vehicle software for this shift.

body.x: Brain-Life Link Pairs Brain Signals With AI in the Focus+ Wearable

Brain-Life Link Joint Stock Company, which co-exhibited at the ASEAN-KOREA STARTUP WEEK 2026 booth at FIX 2026, develops wearable technology that combines a brain-computer interface (BCI) with AI to help users understand their state of focus and mental condition. Its flagship product, Focus+, measures brain activity and bodily responses using electroencephalography (EEG), functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) and photoplethysmography (PPG) signals, and uses AI-based analysis to identify states of concentration and rest.

body.cap: The FIX 2026 Global Media Awards ceremony at the Future Innovation tech eXpo | Photo - AVING News

body.x: Users can check the measured signals in an app and software platform and review their focus flow and recovery state. The product is aimed at everyday settings such as study and work. The company presents Focus+ as consumer technology, not as a medical device for diagnosis or treatment.
Tesollo's DG-5F Robotic Hand Has 20 Degrees of Freedom

Tesollo Inc., led by CEO Youngjin Kim, develops robotic hands and multi-jointed grippers for industrial automation and humanoid robots. Its DG-5F is a five-fingered robotic hand with 20 degrees of freedom (DoF). Each joint is controlled independently, so the hand can grasp and manipulate objects of different shapes.

Founded in 2019, Tesollo makes the Delto Gripper Series in configurations from one to five fingers. The DG-5F family includes the DG-5F-M, for manipulation and research that demand relatively high actuation, and the DG-5F-S, which keeps the 20-DoF structure in a compact body weighing less than 1 kg and is meant for humanoid platforms. The company also supplies SDKs and APIs for connecting the hands to robot arms and AI systems.

body.cap: The FIX 2026 Global Media Awards ceremony at the Future Innovation tech eXpo | Photo - AVING News

body.x: Tesollo's hands and grippers target work that needs delicate handling, such as using tools and assembling and disassembling parts, in addition to gripping objects. According to the company, its products have reached customers in about 20 countries, and Stanford University's HandelBot and DexDrummer research presented in 2026 used the DG-5F-M. Tesollo also won a Best Innovation Technology Award at the FIX 2026 Innovation Awards.

Le Café du Geek's top three span automotive software, a wearable that analyzes brain signals and precision robotic hands.

Ten overseas media outlets from Europe, the Americas and Asia took part in the FIX 2026 Global Media Awards, including Le Café du Geek. Each outlet reviewed the technologies and products of exhibiting companies and chose its own top three. Selected companies gain an opportunity to be publicized through overseas media.

The media partners take part in the FIX 2026 Innovation Awards Media Day and in on-site judging for the BEST OF FIX 2026 Global Media Awards during the show, and plan to report to international audiences on innovative Korean companies in future industries.
